findings.summary: The efficiency gain of Sablewing over Ordell-DDS (50 steps) comes at a sample-quality cost: FID worsens from 7.1 to 7.8, a difference of 0.7 FID points.

sentences.text: On Halvern-Faces 256×256, Sablewing is markedly more efficient than the 50-step Ordell-DDS sampler, requiring 8 versus 50 NFE, 0.94 versus 5.40 TFLOPs per image, and 3.9 versus 21.7 s per batch of 64 images.
This efficiency gain comes at a modest sample-quality cost, with FID increasing from 7.1 for Ordell-DDS to 7.8 for Sablewing.
Compared with the 10-step Ordell-DDS-10, Sablewing is both more efficient (8 vs 10 NFE, 0.94 vs 1.08 TFLOPs, 3.9 vs 4.5 s per batch) and better in quality (FID 7.8 vs 15.6).
No statistical tests were reported, and these results are limited to a single dataset and setting.
